title: UP BOARD CLASS 10 — Biology | Control Coordination Nervous Hormonal
description: Subject-wise test on Control Coordination Nervous Hormonal (Biology) for UP BOARD CLASS 10. 40Q.
subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: What is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system?

options.explanation: Nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.
Neuron is the basic unit of the nervous system.
Axon is a part of a neuron.
Dendrite is a part of a neuron.

questions.explanation: A neuron is the basic unit of the nervous system responsible for transmitting nerve impulses. Nephron is the functional unit of the kidney. Axon and dendrite are parts of a neuron.
questions.hint: It is a specialized cell that transmits nerve impulses.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which plant hormone is primarily responsible for cell elongation in the shoot, leading to stem growth?

options.explanation: Gibberellin promotes stem elongation but is not primarily responsible for cell elongation in the shoot.
Cytokinin promotes cell division but not primarily cell elongation.
Auxin promotes cell elongation in the shoot.
Ethylene is involved in fruit ripening and senescence.

questions.explanation: Auxin is a key plant hormone that promotes cell enlargement, particularly in the shoot, contributing significantly to stem growth and phototropism.
questions.hint: This hormone helps plants grow towards light.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The 'master gland' of the endocrine system, which controls the functioning of many other endocrine glands, is the:

options.explanation: Thyroid gland regulates metabolism.
Adrenal gland regulates stress response.
Pituitary gland is the master gland.
Pancreas regulates blood sugar.

questions.explanation: The pituitary gland secretes several hormones that regulate the activity of other endocrine glands, earning it the title of 'master gland'.
questions.hint: It is located at the base of the brain.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The involuntary and rapid response of the body to a stimulus, occurring without conscious thought, is known as a:

options.explanation: Voluntary actions are under conscious control.
Conditioned reflexes are learned responses.
Reflex actions are involuntary and rapid.
Learned responses are not necessarily involuntary.

questions.explanation: A reflex action is an automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus, often mediated by the spinal cord, allowing for quick protection.
questions.hint: It is an automatic response to avoid harm.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A patient reports symptoms of excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss. These symptoms are characteristic of a deficiency in which hormone?

options.explanation: Thyroxine regulates metabolism.
Adrenaline is involved in the fight-or-flight response.
Insulin regulates blood sugar levels.
Growth hormone regulates growth.

questions.explanation: These symptoms are classic indicators of diabetes mellitus, which is caused by either insufficient production of insulin by the pancreas or the body's inability to use insulin effectively, leading to high blood sugar levels.
questions.hint: This hormone regulates blood sugar levels.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: If a person accidentally touches a hot plate, they immediately withdraw their hand. This quick response is an example of:

options.text: Voluntary action controlled by the cerebrum.
options.explanation: Voluntary actions are under conscious control.

options.text: Reflex action controlled by the spinal cord.
options.explanation: Reflex actions are coordinated by the spinal cord.

options.text: Involuntary action controlled by the cerebellum.
options.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements.

options.text: Conditioned reflex controlled by the medulla.
options.explanation: Conditioned reflexes are learned responses.

questions.explanation: Withdrawing a hand from a hot object is a classic example of a reflex action. These actions are rapid, involuntary, and are primarily coordinated by the spinal cord, without direct involvement of the brain for initial processing.
questions.hint: It is an automatic response to avoid injury.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The bending of a plant shoot towards a source of light is an example of which type of tropism?

options.explanation: Geotropism is growth in response to gravity.
Hydrotropism is growth in response to water.
Phototropism is growth in response to light.
Thigmotropism is growth in response to touch.

questions.explanation: Phototropism is the growth or movement of a plant in response to light. Shoots typically exhibit positive phototropism, growing towards light.
questions.hint: It is a growth response to light.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): The timing and amount of hormone released are precisely regulated in the human body. Reason (R): This regulation is achieved through positive and negative feedback mechanisms.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and R explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Feedback mechanisms, especially negative feedback, are crucial for maintaining hormonal balance by inhibiting further hormone release once a certain level is reached.
questions.hint: Feedback mechanisms help maintain balance in hormone levels.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A person involved in a severe accident suffers damage to a specific part of their brain. Post-recovery, they experience difficulty in maintaining balance while walking and exhibit uncoordinated movements. Which part of the brain was most likely damaged?

options.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for conscious thought and voluntary actions.
The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and balance.
The medulla oblongata controls vital functions like breathing and heartbeat.
The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, and thirst.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is primarily responsible for coordinating voluntary movements, maintaining posture, balance, and equilibrium. Damage to this area would directly result in symptoms like loss of balance and uncoordinated movements.
questions.hint: This part of the brain is responsible for coordination and balance.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately highlights a key difference between nervous control and hormonal control in humans?

options.text: Nervous control is generally slow and its effects are long-lasting, while hormonal control is fast and its effects are short-lived.
options.explanation: Nervous control is fast, and hormonal control is slower.

options.text: Nervous control involves electrical impulses transmitted through neurons, while hormonal control involves chemical messengers transported by the blood.
options.explanation: Nervous control uses electrical impulses, and hormonal control uses chemical messengers.

options.text: Nervous control has widespread effects throughout the body, while hormonal control is highly localized to specific target cells.
options.explanation: Hormonal control can have widespread effects.

options.text: Nervous control is always voluntary, while hormonal control is always involuntary.
options.explanation: Nervous control includes involuntary reflexes.

questions.explanation: Nervous control relies on rapid electrical signals (nerve impulses) transmitted along neurons. Hormonal control, in contrast, uses chemical messengers (hormones) that travel through the bloodstream to target cells, resulting in a slower but often more widespread and long-lasting effect. Option A is incorrect as nervous control is fast. Option C is incorrect as hormones can have widespread effects, and nervous control can also be localized. Option D is incorrect as nervous control includes involuntary reflexes.
questions.hint: Nervous control is fast, while hormonal control is slower but more widespread.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which part of the human brain is responsible for maintaining posture and balance of the body?

options.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for higher brain functions like thought and action.
The medulla oblongata controls autonomic functions such as breathing and heart rate.
Correct. The cerebellum maintains posture and balance.
The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, and thirst.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is primarily responsible for coordinating voluntary movements such as posture, balance, coordination, and speech, resulting in smooth and balanced muscular activity.
questions.hint: This part of the brain is located at the back of the head, under the cerebrum.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The gap between two neurons is called a:

options.explanation: Dendrites are branches of a neuron that receive signals.
An axon is a long projection of a neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body.
Correct. The synapse is the gap between neurons.
The myelin sheath is a fatty layer that insulates axons to speed up signal transmission.

questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrite or cell body of another neuron, across which nerve impulses are transmitted.
questions.hint: This gap allows the transmission of signals between neurons.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following plant hormones promotes cell division?

options.explanation: Auxin promotes cell elongation and root initiation.
Gibberellin promotes stem elongation and seed germination.
Correct. Cytokinin promotes cell division.
Abscisic acid regulates plant stress responses and seed dormancy.

questions.explanation: Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division (cytokinesis) in plant roots and shoots, and also play a role in delaying senescence (aging) in leaves.
questions.hint: This hormone is named after the process it promotes in plant cells.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which endocrine gland is known as the 'master gland' because it controls the activity of other endocrine glands?

options.explanation: The thyroid gland regulates metabolism.
Correct. The pituitary gland is the 'master gland'.
The adrenal gland produces adrenaline and cortisol.
The pancreas regulates blood sugar levels.

questions.explanation: The pituitary gland, located at the base of the brain, secretes hormones that control the functions of other endocrine glands, earning it the title of 'master gland'.
questions.hint: This gland is located near the brain and is crucial for regulating other glands.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A person suddenly withdraws their hand immediately after touching a hot iron. This rapid, involuntary response is an example of a:

options.explanation: Voluntary actions are deliberate and involve conscious thought.
Correct. This is a reflex action.
Hormonal actions involve chemical messengers and are slower.
Conscious actions involve deliberate decision-making.

questions.explanation: A reflex action is an involuntary, almost instantaneous movement in response to a stimulus. It is mediated by a reflex arc, which bypasses the brain for quick processing at the spinal cord level.
questions.hint: This type of action does not involve conscious thought.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Deficiency of iodine in the diet can lead to goitre. Reason (R): Iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroxine hormone by the thyroid gland.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both statements are true, and R explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Thyroxine hormone, produced by the thyroid gland, requires iodine for its synthesis. A deficiency of iodine leads to insufficient thyroxine production, causing the thyroid gland to enlarge in an attempt to produce more hormone, a condition known as goitre.
questions.hint: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the nervous system and hormonal system?

options.text: The nervous system uses electrical impulses and neurotransmitters.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The hormonal system uses chemical messengers called hormones.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The effects of the nervous system are generally slower and long-lasting.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The nervous system's effects are fast and short-lived.

options.text: The hormonal system primarily acts on target organs or cells.
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

questions.explanation: The effects of the nervous system are generally fast and short-lived, as electrical impulses travel rapidly. The hormonal system, on the other hand, typically produces slower but more widespread and long-lasting effects.
questions.hint: The nervous system uses electrical signals, while the hormonal system uses chemical messengers.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A patient reports symptoms of increased blood glucose levels, frequent urination, and excessive thirst. Which of the following hormones is most likely deficient in this patient?

options.explanation: Thyroxine regulates metabolism.
Correct. Insulin deficiency causes diabetes.
Adrenaline is involved in the 'fight or flight' response.
Growth hormone regulates growth and development.

questions.explanation: These symptoms are characteristic of diabetes mellitus, a condition caused by the insufficient production or action of insulin. Insulin is responsible for regulating blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake by cells.
questions.hint: This hormone is produced by the pancreas and regulates blood sugar.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an involuntary action controlled by the hindbrain?

options.explanation: Blood pressure is controlled by the medulla oblongata.
Salivation is controlled by the medulla oblongata.
Correct. Walking is a voluntary action.
Vomiting is controlled by the medulla oblongata.

questions.explanation: Involuntary actions like blood pressure, salivation, and vomiting are controlled by the medulla oblongata in the hindbrain. Walking in a straight line is a voluntary action, though balance (controlled by the cerebellum, also part of the hindbrain) is crucial for it. The act of walking itself is initiated and coordinated by the cerebrum.
questions.hint: Involuntary actions are automatic and do not require conscious thought.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: In plants, the bending of a shoot towards light is due to the uneven distribution of a hormone. This phenomenon is called phototropism. Which hormone is primarily responsible for this, and how does it cause the bending?

options.text: Gibberellin; it promotes cell elongation on the illuminated side.
options.explanation: Gibberellin promotes stem elongation but not phototropism.

options.text: Auxin; it promotes cell elongation on the shaded side.
options.explanation: Correct. Auxin causes cell elongation on the shaded side, leading to bending.

options.text: Cytokinin; it promotes cell division on the illuminated side.
options.explanation: Cytokinin promotes cell division but not phototropism.

options.text: Abscisic acid; it inhibits cell growth on the shaded side.
options.explanation: Abscisic acid inhibits growth but is not involved in phototropism.

questions.explanation: Auxin, a plant hormone, migrates to the shaded side of the shoot when exposed to unilateral light. On the shaded side, a higher concentration of auxin promotes cell elongation, causing the shoot to bend towards the light source (positive phototropism).
questions.hint: This hormone promotes cell elongation and is involved in plant growth responses.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which gland is responsible for regulating metabolism in the human body by secreting thyroxin hormone?

options.explanation: The adrenal gland secretes hormones like adrenaline and cortisol, not thyroxin.
The pituitary gland is the master gland but does not secrete thyroxin.
Correct. The thyroid gland secretes thyroxin hormone.
The pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon, not thyroxin.

questions.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxin hormone, which plays a crucial role in regulating the body's metabolism, growth, and development.
questions.hint: This gland is located in the neck region.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The longest part of a neuron, which transmits nerve impulses away from the cell body towards other neurons or effectors, is called the:

options.explanation: Dendrites receive nerve impulses, they do not transmit them away.
Correct. The axon transmits nerve impulses away from the cell body.
A synapse is the gap between neurons, not a part of the neuron itself.
The cyton contains the nucleus but does not transmit impulses away.

questions.explanation: The axon is the long, slender projection of a neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the neuron's cell body. Dendrites receive impulses, and the cyton contains the nucleus.
questions.hint: This part is responsible for sending signals to other cells.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the path of a nerve impulse in a typical reflex arc?

options.text: Receptor → Motor neuron → Sensory neuron → Effector → Spinal cord
options.explanation: This sequence is incorrect as the sensory neuron comes before the motor neuron.

options.text: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Effector
options.explanation: Correct. This is the proper sequence in a reflex arc.

options.text: Effector → Motor neuron → Spinal cord → Sensory neuron → Receptor
options.explanation: This sequence is reversed and incorrect.

options.text: Sensory neuron → Receptor → Spinal cord → Motor neuron → Effector
options.explanation: The receptor comes before the sensory neuron, so this sequence is incorrect.

questions.explanation: In a reflex arc, the impulse is first detected by a receptor, then transmitted by a sensory neuron to the spinal cord (CNS), from there to a motor neuron, and finally to an effector organ (like a muscle or gland) to produce a response.
questions.hint: The sequence starts with the receptor and ends with the effector.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A plant seedling bends towards a light source. This phenomenon is primarily controlled by the uneven distribution of which plant hormone?

options.explanation: Gibberellin promotes stem elongation but is not primarily responsible for phototropism.
Cytokinin promotes cell division but does not control phototropism.
Abscisic acid is involved in stress responses and seed dormancy, not phototropism.
Correct. Auxin controls phototropism by uneven distribution.

questions.explanation: Auxin is a plant hormone responsible for cell elongation. When light falls on one side of the shoot, auxin migrates to the shaded side, causing cells on that side to elongate more rapidly, leading to the bending of the shoot towards light (phototropism).
questions.hint: This hormone is involved in cell elongation and phototropism.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Insulin hormone, which regulates blood sugar levels, is secreted by which endocrine gland?

options.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxin, not insulin.
The adrenal gland secretes adrenaline and cortisol, not insulin.
Correct. The pancreas secretes insulin.
The pituitary gland is the master gland but does not secrete insulin.

questions.explanation: The pancreas is an endocrine gland that secretes insulin (which lowers blood sugar) and glucagon (which raises blood sugar) to maintain glucose homeostasis in the body.
questions.hint: This gland is located near the stomach.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Deficiency of iodine in the diet can lead to a condition called goitre. Reason (R): Iodine is an essential mineral required for the synthesis of thyroxin hormone by the thyroid gland.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both statements are true, and R explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true. Goitre is caused by an enlarged thyroid gland due to insufficient production of thyroxin. Thyroxin synthesis requires iodine, so a deficiency of iodine directly leads to reduced thyroxin production, causing the thyroid gland to enlarge in an attempt to produce more hormone.
questions.hint: The reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A person met with an accident and suffered damage to a part of their brain. As a result, they are unable to maintain balance while walking and have difficulty coordinating voluntary movements. Which part of the brain is most likely affected?

options.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for higher brain functions like thinking and memory, not balance.
Correct. The cerebellum controls balance and coordination.
The medulla oblongata controls vital functions like breathing and heartbeat, not balance.
The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, and thirst, not balance.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the part of the hindbrain responsible for coordinating voluntary movements, maintaining posture, balance, and equilibrium. Damage to the cerebellum typically results in problems with coordination and balance.
questions.hint: This part of the brain is located at the back, under the cerebrum.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: The microscopic gap that exists between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrite or cell body of another neuron, across which nerve impulses are transmitted, is called a:

options.explanation: A dendrite is a part of the neuron that receives signals, not a gap.
An axon is a part of the neuron that transmits signals, not a gap.
Correct. A synapse is the gap between neurons.
The myelin sheath is a fatty layer that insulates the axon, not a gap.

questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction between two nerve cells, consisting of a minute gap across which impulses pass by diffusion of a neurotransmitter.
questions.hint: This gap is where neurotransmitters are released.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A patient is diagnosed with abnormally high blood sugar levels. The doctor prescribes medication to stimulate the production of a particular hormone to bring the sugar levels down. Which hormone is the doctor trying to increase, and from which gland is it secreted?

options.explanation: Thyroxin regulates metabolism, not blood sugar levels.
Adrenaline increases blood sugar levels, it does not lower them.
Correct. Insulin lowers blood sugar levels and is secreted by the pancreas.
Growth hormone regulates growth, not blood sugar levels.

questions.explanation: High blood sugar levels (hyperglycemia) are a characteristic of diabetes. Insulin, secreted by the pancreas, is the hormone responsible for lowering blood glucose by promoting its uptake by cells and conversion to glycogen. Therefore, the doctor would aim to increase insulin production or its action.
questions.hint: This hormone is secreted by the pancreas.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: When the roots of a plant grow downwards into the soil in response to gravity, and the shoot grows upwards towards the light, these specific responses are examples of:

options.explanation: Hydrotropism is a response to water, not gravity.
Correct. Roots show geotropism (response to gravity), and shoots show phototropism (response to light).
Chemotropism is a response to chemicals, and thigmotropism is a response to touch, neither fits the given scenario.
Hydrotropism is a response to water, not light.

questions.explanation: The growth of roots downwards in response to gravity is called positive geotropism. The growth of shoots upwards towards light is called positive phototropism.
questions.hint: Geotropism is a response to gravity, and phototropism is a response to light.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which part of the human brain is responsible for maintaining balance and posture?

options.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for higher brain functions like thought and action.
Correct. The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements, balance, and posture.
The medulla oblongata controls autonomic functions like breathing and heart rate.
The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, and hormone release.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain and is responsible for coordinating voluntary movements, balance, and posture.
questions.hint: This part of the brain is located at the back and is involved in motor control.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males during puberty?

options.explanation: Estrogen is the primary female sex hormone.
Progesterone is a female hormone involved in the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.
Correct. Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone.
Insulin regulates blood sugar levels.

questions.explanation: Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone responsible for the development of male secondary sexual characteristics such as facial hair, deepening of the voice, and muscle growth.
questions.hint: This hormone is produced in the testes and is crucial for male development.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Assertion: The spinal cord is responsible for reflex actions. Reason: Reflex actions are quick, involuntary responses to stimuli that are processed in the spinal cord.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.explanation: The reason is also true.

options.text: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The spinal cord acts as the center for reflex actions. The quick, involuntary response to stimuli is processed in the spinal cord, making both the assertion and reason correct, with the reason correctly explaining the assertion.
questions.hint: Reflex actions are rapid and do not involve conscious thought.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following glands is both endocrine and exocrine in function?

options.explanation: The pituitary gland is purely endocrine.
The thyroid gland is purely endocrine.
Correct. The pancreas has both endocrine and exocrine functions.
The adrenal gland is purely endocrine.

questions.explanation: The pancreas acts as an exocrine gland by secreting digestive enzymes into the small intestine and as an endocrine gland by releasing hormones like insulin and glucagon into the bloodstream.
questions.hint: This gland has dual roles in digestion and hormone secretion.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: A student accidentally touches a hot object and immediately withdraws his hand. This response is an example of:

options.explanation: Voluntary actions require conscious thought.
Correct. This is an involuntary reflex action.
Hormonal actions involve chemical messengers like hormones.
Sensory actions involve the detection of stimuli, not the response.

questions.explanation: Withdrawing the hand from a hot object is an involuntary action, also known as a reflex action, which is processed by the spinal cord without conscious thought.
questions.hint: This type of action does not require conscious decision-making.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the adrenal glands and helps the body respond to stress?

options.explanation: Thyroxine regulates metabolism.
Correct. Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands and helps the body respond to stress.
Growth hormone regulates growth and metabolism.
Insulin regulates blood sugar levels.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline, also known as epinephrine, is secreted by the adrenal glands and plays a key role in the body's 'fight or flight' response to stress by increasing heart rate and blood pressure.
questions.hint: This hormone is often called the 'stress hormone.'
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Case-Based: A person experiences symptoms such as frequent urination, excessive thirst, and fatigue. The doctor suspects a hormonal imbalance. Which hormone is most likely deficient in this person?

options.explanation: Thyroxine regulates metabolism.
Correct. Insulin deficiency leads to diabetes, causing the described symptoms.
Growth hormone regulates growth and metabolism.
Adrenaline is involved in the stress response.

questions.explanation: The symptoms described are characteristic of diabetes, which is caused by a deficiency in insulin, a hormone produced by the pancreas that regulates blood sugar levels.
questions.hint: This hormone is crucial for regulating blood glucose levels.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the function of the hypothalamus?

options.explanation: Voluntary actions are controlled by the cerebrum.

options.text: It regulates body temperature and hunger.
options.explanation: Correct. The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, and thirst.

options.text: It is responsible for auditory and visual processing.
options.explanation: Auditory and visual processing occur in the cerebrum.

options.text: It secretes all the hormones in the body.
options.explanation: The hypothalamus controls hormone release but does not secrete all hormones.

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is a region of the brain that plays a crucial role in maintaining homeostasis, including regulating body temperature, hunger, and thirst, and controlling the release of hormones from the pituitary gland.
questions.hint: This part of the brain is involved in maintaining internal balance.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: During the menstrual cycle, which hormone is responsible for the thickening of the uterine lining?

options.explanation: FSH stimulates follicle development in the ovaries.
LH triggers ovulation and the formation of the corpus luteum.
Correct. Estrogen thickens the uterine lining.
Progesterone maintains the uterine lining after ovulation.

questions.explanation: Estrogen is secreted by the developing follicle in the ovary and is responsible for the thickening of the uterine lining (endometrium) in preparation for a potential pregnancy.
questions.hint: This hormone is produced by the ovaries and prepares the uterus for pregnancy.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the central nervous system?

options.explanation: The brain is part of the central nervous system.
The spinal cord is part of the central nervous system.
Correct. Nerves are part of the peripheral nervous system.
Cerebrospinal fluid surrounds and protects the CNS.

questions.explanation: The central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord. Nerves are part of the peripheral nervous system (PNS), which connects the CNS to the rest of the body.
questions.hint: The CNS includes only the brain and spinal cord.
questions.subject: upbo10-biology
